arxiv-2202-02225.title: A Markov Chain Surrogate Model for a Two-Dimensional Interacting Particle System with Internal Collisions Thanks:
arxiv-2202-02225.creator: Tricity Andrew, James D. Nance, Mansoor A. Haider
arxiv-2202-02225.description: Abstract A probabilistic Markov Chain (MC) surrogate model for a two-dimensional system of interacting particles within a square domain having inherent symmetries is developed. Particles are assumed to be circular and identical, colliding with each other and with rigid domain walls via perfectly elastic collisions. Simulation results over many realizations are used to develop and evaluate the surrogate MC model.

arxiv-2301-03589.title: Explainable, Physics Aware, Trustworthy AI Paradigm Shift for Synthetic Aperture Radar
arxiv-2301-03589.creator: Mihai Datcu, Zhongling Huang, Andrei Anghel, Juanping Zhao, Remus Cacoveanu
arxiv-2301-03589.description: Abstract The recognition or understanding of the scenes observed with a SAR system requires a broader range of cues, beyond the spatial context. These encompass but are not limited to: imaging geometry, imaging mode, properties of the Fourier spectrum of the images or the behavior of the polarimetric signatures.

arxiv-2303-11401.title: Closed vortex state in 3D mesoscopic superconducting films under an applied transport current
arxiv-2303-11401.creator: Leonardo Rodrigues Cadorim, Lucas Veneziani de Toledo, Wilson Aires Ortiz, Jorge Berger, Edson Sardella
arxiv-2303-11401.description: Abstract By using the full 3D generalized time dependent Ginzbug-Landau equation we study a long superconducting film of finite width and thickness under an applied transport current. We show that, for sufficiently large thickness, the vortices and the antivortices become curved before they annihilate each other.

arxiv-2407-21005.title: Settling the Pass Complexity of Approximate Matchings in Dynamic Graph Streams
arxiv-2407-21005.creator: Sepehr Assadi, Soheil Behnezhad, Christian Konrad, Kheeran K. Naidu, Janani Sundaresan
arxiv-2407-21005.description: Abstract A semi-streaming algorithm in dynamic graph streams processes any n n -vertex graph by making one or multiple passes over a stream of insertions and deletions to edges of the graph and using O ​ ( n ⋅ polylog ​ ( n ) ) O(n\cdot\mbox{\rm polylog}{(n)}) space.

arxiv-2410-01766.title: SegHeD: Segmentation of Heterogeneous Data for Multiple Sclerosis Lesions with Anatomical Constraints
arxiv-2410-01766.creator: Berke Doga Basaran (✉), Xinru Zhang, Paul M. Matthews, Wenjia Bai
arxiv-2410-01766.description: Abstract Assessment of lesions and their longitudinal progression from brain magnetic resonance (MR) images plays a crucial role in diagnosing and monitoring multiple sclerosis (MS). Machine learning models have demonstrated a great potential for automated MS lesion segmentation. Training such models typically requires large-scale high-quality datasets that are consistently annotated.

arxiv-2410-22787.title: Mimetic Weyl geometric gravity
arxiv-2410-22787.creator: Daria-Ioana Vișa, Tiberiu Harko, Shahab Shahidi
arxiv-2410-22787.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daria-Ioana Vișa, Tiberiu Harko, Shahab Shahidi. We consider a mimetic type extension of the Weyl geometric gravity theory, by assuming that the metric of the space-time manifold can be parameterized in terms of a scalar field, called the mimetic field. The action of the model is obtained by starting from a conformally invariant gravitational action, constructed, in Weyl geometry, from the square of the Weyl scalar, the strength of the Weyl vector, and an effective matter term, respectively.

arxiv-2507-22557.title: Effects of strong turbulence for water waves
arxiv-2507-22557.creator: E.A. Kochurin, E.A. Kuznetsov
arxiv-2507-22557.description: Abstract The results of direct numerical simulation of plane-symmetric turbulence of water waves for potential flows within the framework of conformal variables taking into account low-frequency pumping and high-frequency viscous dissipation are presented. In this model, for a wide range of pumping amplitudes, the weak turbulence regime was not detected.

pmc-11860174.title: Changes in brain structure and function in youth at familial risk for schizophrenia or bipolar disorder: implications for early intervention
pmc-11860174.creator: G Sugranyes, BASYS Working Group
pmc-11860174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-13297882.title: A Prognostic Model Incorporating Age and Systemic Inflammation Response Index for Primary CNS Lymphoma
pmc-13297882.creator: Ryosuke Matsuda, Takeshi Okuda, Hiromasa Yoshioka, Kengo Yamada, Takayuki Morimoto, Tsutomu Nakazawa, Hiromichi Hayami, Ryosuke Maeoka, Shohei Yokoyama, Ichiro Nakagawa
pmc-13297882.description: Simple SummaryPrimary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is an aggressive brain tumor for which accurate prognostic assessment is essential for treatment planning. Existing prognostic models often require clinical or laboratory parameters that are not always readily available in routine practice.

pmc-13338433.title: Physics-informed deep learning-based adaptive beamforming for phased array weather radar
pmc-13338433.creator: Tarek Sallam, Ahmed M. Attiya
pmc-13338433.description: This study introduces a beamforming framework based on physics-informed deep-learning for phased array weather radar systems, with particular emphasis on configurations involving a large number of antenna elements. The proposed approach is designed to achieve both high computational efficiency and reliable weather target detection.

pmc-13549923.title: Acute and Chronic Pancreatitis in Mitochondrial Disease: A Systematic Review
pmc-13549923.creator: Olivia Hahl, Mika H. Martikainen
pmc-13549923.description: Mitochondrial disease is a common inherited multisystem neurometabolic disorder. Pancreatic dysfunction is a recognised manifestation, most frequently presenting as mitochondrial diabetes. Although pancreatitis cases have been reported in association with mitochondrial disease, acute and chronic pancreatitis in this context remain poorly characterised.
